polynomial_end_behavior.display_name: Determine end behavior of a polynomial

easy.statement_latex: Describe the end behavior of $p(x) = 2x^{4} + 4x^{3} + x^{2} + 3x - 2$.
easy.answer_latex: As $x \to +\infty$, $p(x) \to +\infty$; as $x \to -\infty$, $p(x) \to +\infty$.
hints: End behavior depends only on the leading term of the polynomial.
If the degree is even, both ends of the graph go in the same direction. If the degree is odd, the ends go opposite ways.
A positive leading coefficient leaves the graph un-flipped; a negative leading coefficient reflects it.
solution_steps_latex: Identify the leading term: $2x^{4}$.
The degree is $4$ (even) and the leading coefficient is $2$ (positive).
Because the degree is even, both ends of the graph head the same way.
Because the leading coefficient is positive, the graph is not reflected.
Therefore as $x \to +\infty$, $p(x) \to +\infty$; and as $x \to -\infty$, $p(x) \to +\infty$.
